Build the base matrices of the GGM precision predictor

Source: R/ggm_layer.R
mc_precision_bases.Rd

Constructs the base matrices \(Z_d\) of the linear-in-precision predictor of the Gaussian graphical model (GGM) layer, $$K_b = \sum_{d=1}^{q_{\mathcal G}} \eta_d Z_d,\qquad \Sigma_b = K_b^{-1},$$ where \(K_b\) is the between-response precision matrix and \(q_{\mathcal G} = R + |E|\) is the number of graph parameters. There are \(R\) diagonal bases \(Z_{kk} = e_k e_k^\top\) and one symmetric base \(Z_{ij} = e_i e_j^\top + e_j e_i^\top\) per edge \((i, j)\), so that \(\eta_{kk} = [K_b]_{kk}\) and \(\eta_{ij} = [K_b]_{ij}\). The pair \((i, j)\) is conditionally independent given the other responses, in the Gaussian sense, exactly when it is outside the edge set (Dempster, 1972; Lauritzen, 1996).

Usage

mc_precision_bases(R, edges = NULL)

Arguments

R

integer, number of responses (\(R \ge 2\)).

edges

optional integer matrix with two columns giving the edges \((i, j)\), \(i < j\), as response positions in 1:R. If NULL, the complete graph is used; a matrix with no rows is the empty graph. The edges are stored sorted in lexicographic order, which is the order of the edge parameters.

Value

An object of class "mcg_bases": a list with components bases (list of \(q_{\mathcal G}\) symmetric \(R \times R\) matrices), cube (the same bases as an \(R \times R \times q_{\mathcal G}\) array, the form consumed by the C++ kernels), names (parameter names eta_kk and eta_ij), type ("diag" or "edge" for each base), edges (the canonical edge matrix) and R.

References

Dempster, A. P. (1972). Covariance selection. Biometrics, 28(1), 157-175. doi:10.2307/2528966

Lauritzen, S. L. (1996). Graphical Models. Oxford University Press.

See also

mc_build_precision, mc_between_graph

Other GGM layer: mc_build_precision(), mc_check_spd(), mc_precision_derivatives(), mc_precision_to_covariance(), mc_spd_line_search()

Examples

b <- mc_precision_bases(3)
length(b$bases)            # 3 diagonal + 3 edges = 6
#> [1] 6
mc_precision_bases(3, edges = rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)))$names
#> [1] "eta_11" "eta_22" "eta_33" "eta_12" "eta_23"
